text:
The Division of Highways has authority to negotiate the purchase of lands for borrow pits. However, leaving the sources of materials up to the contractors has proven to be advantageous to all. All borrow pits whether in view of a public road or not, will be topsoiled, fertilized and seeded.
All lands acquired by the proposed facility which are not needed for actual construction of the pavement will be landscaped to provide a primary ground cover. Landscaping contracts will be let after the roadway work is completed to establish shrubs and trees.
Other protective measures that will be incorporated into the actual roadway plans are listed below:
1. All areas disturbed for construction purposes that are not paved will be covered with 4 inches of topsoil and established with grasses.
2. Slopes greater than 2 1/2 to 1, as under bridges, will be permanently paved by an asphalt or concrete method.
3. Erosion prevention aprons will be placed at culvert pipe discharges. Concrete flumes will be placed in areas of concentrated runoff.
4. For protection of ditches and earth embankments erosion prevention matting, sod and mulch will be provided.
5. Selected grasses, tree and shrub plantings will provide a highway landscape which will be aesthetically pleasing.
6. Altered drainage patterns will have adequate ditches and culverts.
